# Welcome

Welcome to the online site for Geog4/6300: Data Science in Geography. This course is offered each fall within the University of Georgia's Department of Geography. It provides a review/introduction to both geostatistical analysis and to using a code-based approach (specifically using R) for doing quantitative research. 

This course is NOT a GIS class, but we will cover how to load and work with spatial data and use elements of spatial analysis. It spends more time on data cleaning and manipulation that most GIS coursework as well as reviewing statistical techniques such as tests of difference and regression modeling.

# Where to find things

* The [course syllabus](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C1GHXTsvwvRl92LuJcXnIIgqvD3WQ9tmZ1REM0LTE_I/edit?usp=drive_link){target="_blank"} and [schedule](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1kkK6xVx-wwIya_0yzGHPzkEqEGFJWAxO41vaOcfqs4Y/edit?usp=drive_link){target="_blank"} are both hosted on Google Drive. Click the links to find those. 
* The main content of the course is broken into [modules](modules/index.qmd), and this site will provide a page with resources relevant to each of them. This includes links to relevant scripts and datasets used in class. These are also available on the Github repository linked to this site. Click the Github link in the top menu bar for another way to find those.
* For lab assignments, we are using [Github Classroom](https://classroom.github.com/){target="_blank"}. This systems allows you to easily "fork" the lab--creating your own copy--and then submit once you are finished. Click on the Labs link in the top menu bar to see links to each assignment. 
* [ELC](https://elc.uga.edu){target="_blank"} will be the place to go for recordings of our class sessions as well as things related to assessment.
* The [Resources](resources.qmd) page of this site has multiple online guides to help support your work and learning.
* We will also often be using the [Tidy Tuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday){target="_blank"} repository for in-class activities and group work.
